newsitem.title: UK: Softs outlook - Volatile coffee seen correcting lower.
newsitem.headline: Softs outlook - Volatile coffee seen correcting lower.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures are expected to dominate attention on London's soft commodity markets this week as traders nervously await a downward correction after last week's meteoric rally.
White sugar futures are expected to hold steady and even claw their way higher as May arbitrage shorts cover positions before the March raws expiry in New York.
The cocoa market is still trapped under a long-term downtrend but appears to be struggling higher.

Last week's surging arabicas market pushed London coffee into heavily overbought territory but with profits likely to be taken at some stage prices still have upside potential and could hit $1,800 basis May, traders said.
"We've been looking for a retracement for some time now," said one analyst.
Although New York will be closed for President's Day on Monday, robusta traders should have plenty of data from which to extract clues on nearby availability and the size of speculative positions.
Traders said the rise could make the market increasingly wary of a speculative ambush to tap the 40 percent jump in prices since early January.
They will also be looking for clues on roaster interest in the past two weeks and monitor Tuesday's U.S. green coffee data, expected to show an increase.
Also being watched is the Colombian public sector strike, which enters its seventh day on Monday after talks between unions and government ministers ended in deadlock last week.
In white sugar, traders said they expected values to hold steady if not move slightly higher -- although the focus of London interest would be the approaching March raws expiry in New York.
The expected firmness on the whites market would pressure nearby white/raw differentials, especially as holders of short positions would have to cover.
"There are still a few people who are quite short of the premium so you might find that at some stage they will have to look to liquidate," said one trader.

Traders said London's May contract, now spot position after last week's March expiry, was likely to hold above $300.00 support although Asian offtake from Pakistan and Indonesia could still have a bullish knock-on effect.
"The whites may hold around these levels and maybe try and move up a little, depending on whether the offtake increases or keeps going like it has done."
In cocoa, traders said the market was still trapped in the shadow of a long-term downtrend but was making efforts to rally.

London's May contract skidded to score a series of life-of-contract lows last week, although analysts said the fact that the continuation support level of 847 stg managed to hold was probably a bullish sign.

Traders said while fund players were short and would have to buy at some point, they were unlikely to be in a rush to boost values. But industry buyers would be lured to the market if sterling's weakness continued.
"I think it's just going to drift," said one, while another saw the market's likely progress as very much dictated by New York.
No one was prepared to predict a sharp move. "I can't see it going much lower...but it's hard to see where the support is coming from," the first said.

Elsewhere, West African cocoa arrivals are nearing last year's record and good prospects for the Ivorian mid crop have recently caused more bearish sentiment, although some traders suggested origins were now oversold.
Ghana's latest weekly arrivals are due this week.
